messages.author: 9b1f1220a2b07d1e
messages.subject: Re: experience with dDHMM
parts:
Hi Tim--

Thanks for sending along the code and data. The "bad parameters for distribution" error you're getting has to do with the argument "checkRowSums," which needs to be provided either as 1 (in which case the dDHMM will check whether row probabilities of your S and O arrays are valid, which is safer but slower) or 0 (in which case probabilities won't be checked, which is faster).

Once you provide that argument, you'll also need to make sure your dimensions are all correct. probObs should be (S x O) and probTrans should be (S x S x T-1) where S is the number of possible system states, O is the number of possible observation states, and T is the length of the data vector S. It looks like the documentation erroneously says that dim(probTrans)[3] can be larger than T-1, but we changed that so I've made a note to correct that in the documentation. Apologies for the confusion.

The version I have that doesn't throw an error is the following, but you should double check that this is actually what you want.

    Y[i,2:n.occasions]~dDHMM(init=i.probs[i,1:3],
                 probObs=O[1:n.states,1:obs.states],
                 probTrans=S[1:n.states,1:n.states,2:(n.occasions-1)],
                 len=n.occasions-1,
                 checkRowSums = 1)

There are some unrelated warnings that get thrown with this version, so let me know if you have any additional questions.

Seems like the mailing list might be on a delay today so apologies if we crossed emails!

Best,
Ben
